name: New York Department of Financial Services

summary.text: The New York State Department of Financial Services was created in 2011 under the Financial Services Law by merging the state's Banking and Insurance Departments, which were abolished on October 3, 2011. Its website says it regulates more than 3,000 financial institutions with nearly $10 trillion in assets, including more than 1,900 insurers and more than 1,300 banks and other financial institutions such as credit unions, money services businesses and student loan servicers. On this site it appears through its two consent orders with Deutsche Bank: the $425 million penalty of January 30, 2017 over the Russian mirror-trading scheme and the $150 million penalty of July 7, 2020 over the bank's relationships with Jeffrey Epstein, Danske Estonia and FBME Bank.

facts.claim: On January 30, 2017 DFS fined Deutsche Bank $425 million under a consent order over a 'mirror trading' scheme that moved $10 billion out of Russia, and required the bank to engage an independent monitor.
facts.quote: The bank allowed traders to engage in a money-laundering scheme using "mirror trades" that improperly shifted $10 billion out of Russia.

sources.publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services
sources.title: DFS Fines Deutsche Bank $425 Million for Russian Mirror-Trading Scheme

facts.claim: On July 7, 2020 DFS announced a $150 million penalty on Deutsche Bank AG, its New York branch and Deutsche Bank Trust Company America under a consent order concerning the bank's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and its correspondent relationships with Danske Bank Estonia and FBME Bank.
facts.quote: Deutsche Bank AG, its New York branch, and Deutsche Bank Trust Company America (collectively "Deutsche Bank" or the "Bank") have agreed to pay $150 million in penalties
